ingredients.name: Ridge gourd (watakolu / luffa)
ingredients.notes: peeled (only the dark green ridges; leave the inner pale green skin), halved, seeds removed, cut into 3-4cm diagonal pieces. Always taste a small raw piece first -- occasionally ridge gourd is bitter, which means it is overripe and should be discarded.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: juiced; added at the end, optional but brightens the dish

steps.instruction: Peel the ridge gourd using a vegetable peeler or knife, removing only the dark green ridged skin while keeping the paler green inner skin -- this gives the curry its colour and extra flavour. Halve lengthways, scoop out the seeds with a spoon, then cut diagonally into 3-4cm pieces. Always taste a small raw piece before cooking; occasionally ridge gourd is bitter which means it has over-ripened and should not be used.

Place the prepared ridge gourd pieces in a pot along with the onion, green chillies, garlic, curry leaves, pandan leaf, cinnamon stick, fenugreek, turmeric, curry powder, Maldive fish flakes (if using), and salt.

Pour in the thin coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Cook uncovered for about 15-20 minutes on low heat, stirring occasionally, until the ridge gourd is completely tender. Low, slow cooking allows the cinnamon to properly infuse.
Pour in the thick coconut milk. Stir gently and bring back just to a simmer -- do not let it boil hard. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly.
Stir in the lime juice (if using). Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot with plain rice alongside a spicier meat or fish curry to balance this very mild dish.

source_site: hungrylankan.com, cross-checked against foodcnr.com, cinnamonvogue.com, agfg.com.au (Peter Kuruvita), siddhalepa.com, akkiskitchen.com, grandmamenu.com, and limitlessspice.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 8+ independent sources; strong agreement on the very mild white-curry style and the importance of tasting raw ridge gourd for bitterness before cooking
notes: Watakolu curry is described across multiple sources as a 'comfort food' curry -- extremely mild, light, and easy to digest, making it a popular choice when feeling unwell. Unlike most Sri Lankan curries in this collection, it uses no chilli powder and only green chillies for a very gentle heat. The bitterness check before cooking is unusual for a vegetable dish but consistently recommended: very ripe or overgrown ridge gourd can be intensely bitter -- the same issue as bitter gourd (sl_028) but less predictable, as ridge gourd is not meant to be bitter at all. Ceylon cinnamon is highlighted by several sources (notably cinnamonvogue.com, written by a cinnamon brand) as more appropriate than cassia for this mild curry, as it gives a subtler, fruitier background note without dominating. The vegetable is also known as luffa, Chinese okra, and turai in other Asian cuisines.
